content.text: ▪︎often assoc w/ rosacea or seborrheic dermatitis
: inflam of the anterior eyelid margins involving skin, eyelashes, & follicles
: inflam of the posterior eyelid margins assoc w/
red, swollen eyelids w/ crusting/scaling on eyelid margin & eyelashes
▪︎eye irritate (ex, pain, itching, FB sensation, watering)
(ex, warm compress, washing w/ baby shampoo, ⍉contacts/makeup)
▪︎oral abx (tetracyclines) reserved for severe or refractory cases
: outward folding of eyelid (USU lower eyelid)
laxity of tarsal plates & canthal tendons
orbicularis oculi paralysis d/t facial n. palsy
laxity of tarsal plates, canthal tendons, &
trichiasis (inward growth of eyelashes), FB sensation, epiphora (watering), red eye
: artificial tears, ocular lubricants @ night, soft contact lenses to protect cornea;
▪︎acute inflam of the tear gland or eyelash follicles
: Moll’s or Zeis gland @ lid margin
▪︎external: grows from the base of the eyelash; internal: located beneath the eyelid
▪︎topical abx often used but have little benefit
ophthalmology Refer for topical ABX/steroid combo, I&D
▪︎MC above the eyelashes on the upper lid
▪︎typically painless, often subacute presentation (vs hordeolum: painful + tender)
